What to look for in adventure helmets

  • Fit first. The safest helmet is one that fits your head shape snugly with no pressure points — try several brands before buying.
  • Look for ECE 22.06. The current safety standard includes rotational-impact testing. A high SHARP star rating is a useful extra guide.
  • Pinlock-ready visor. Essential for the UK — a Pinlock insert stops fogging on cold, damp mornings.
  • Weight matters. Under ~1,600g keeps neck fatigue down on long days. Composite and carbon shells are lighter than polycarbonate.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on adventure helmets?

Our catalogue spans £184.99 to £399.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include LS2. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Are expensive helmets actually safer?

Not necessarily — every road-legal helmet meets the same ECE 22.06 standard. You pay more for lighter materials, lower noise, better ventilation and comfort features, not a higher safety floor. Always prioritise correct fit.

faq.q: What makes an adventure helmet different?
faq.a: Adventure and dual-sport helmets pair a full-face shell with a sun peak and usually a larger eye port, so they suit both tarmac and light off-road riding. Many, like the LS2 Advant X and Advant II, add a flip-up chin bar. The peak shades your eyes and blocks roost off-road, and the wide aperture leaves room for goggles.

faq.q: Can I use goggles with an ADV helmet?
faq.a: Yes, the generous eye port on ADV helmets is designed to fit motocross-style goggles for dusty or muddy trail sections. On the road you can drop the visor and use the internal sun visor instead. Many riders keep goggles for green lanes and rely on the visor for road miles, swapping as the terrain changes.

faq.q: Is the peak a problem on the motorway?
faq.a: At sustained high speed the peak can catch the wind and cause buffeting or lift, which becomes tiring. If you do a lot of motorway distance, choose a helmet with a removable or vented peak so you can take it off for long tarmac stints. Several LS2 Advant models allow the peak and visor to be reconfigured.

faq.q: Are carbon adventure helmets worth the extra?
faq.a: The LS2 Advant X Carbon costs more than the composite Advant models but uses a carbon shell to shave weight. For long days in the saddle, especially standing on the pegs off-road, lower weight noticeably reduces neck fatigue. If your riding is mostly road-based, the standard composite shells offer the same ECE 22.06 safety floor for less.

faq.q: Do adventure helmets meet the same safety standard?
faq.a: Yes, all four of our LS2 picks are built to ECE 22.06, the same standard as road and touring helmets. The dual-homologated modular versions are certified for use with the chin bar up or down. As with any helmet, prioritise a snug, even fit with no pressure points, since fit is what determines real-world protection.
